notes.provenance: REAL capture via tools/gen-schema-v2-fixtures.mjs. The abort is genuine, not simulated: the generator calls neither endTrial() nor stopSession(), then serializes — which is what a closed tab leaves behind. serialize()'s `state.endReason || 'aborted'` is the line that turns an unstopped session into this file.
notes.what_this_fixture_is_for: `end_reason: "aborted"` had no fixture: canonical-core, jspsych-full and every other generated entry state "finished", so the enum's other inhabited value was never loaded by either player. §2 types it as a four-way union and §11 asks strict validation to check every declared field; an enum with one witness is a check nobody has watched discriminate.
notes.t_end_is_NOT_null_and_that_is_a_finding: THE SPEC APPENDIX ASKS THIS FIXTURE FOR 'end_reason aborted, OPEN SEGMENT (t_end: null)' AND CH CANNOT PRODUCE THE SECOND HALF. §3 types t_end as 'null if segment open at recording end', but src/replay/serializer.js closes every segment deliberately — `t_end: wireT(trial.tEnd != null ? trial.tEnd : lastEventT, s0)` — so a segment still open at serialization time is written as ending at its last observed event (here 44.5, the dom.add). The spot check above pins the non-null value rather than papering over it, and `segment-bounds.json` carries the `t_end: null` case hand-authored, because the format's open-segment reading needs a witness and CH is not able to be one. ROUTED TO r3: either §3 gains a sentence permitting a producer to close an open segment at its last event (and CH is conforming), or it does not (and CH's serializer changes). The two fixtures together are what makes that a decision rather than an oversight.
notes.no_redaction_leak: Holds vacuously — nothing here is redacted.
